text: 📘 The Concept of Money 1. Introduction ●​ Money is a universal medium of exchange that facilitates trade, eliminates the inefficiencies of barter, and serves as a foundation for modern economies. ●​ It is not just coins and notes, but also digital balances, credit, and even emerging forms like cryptocurrency. 2. Functions of Money ●​ Medium of Exchange: Enables transactions without direct barter. ●​ Unit of Account: Provides a standard measure of value. ●​ Store of Value: Preserves purchasing

of value. ●​ Store of Value: Preserves purchasing power over time. ●​ Standard of Deferred Payment: Allows contracts and loans to be settled in the future. 3. Evolution of Money ●​ Barter System: Direct exchange of goods/services. ●​ Commodity Money: Items like gold, silver, salt, or cattle. ●​ Metallic Coins: Durable, portable, and widely accepted. ●​ Paper Money: Promissory notes backed by governments. ●​ Bank Money: Checks, drafts, and deposits. ●​ Electronic Money: Debit cards, online

●​ Electronic Money: Debit cards, online transfers. ●​ Cryptocurrency: Decentralized digital assets like Bitcoin. 4. Types of Money Type Description Example Fiat Money Issued by governments, not backed by physical assets USD, INR Commodity Money Value derived from material Gold coins Fiduciary Money Based on trust, not intrinsic value Banknotes Commercial Bank Money Created through lending Deposits Digital Money Exists electronically PayPal, UPI Cryptocurrency Blockchain-based decentralized

Characteristics of Good Money ●​ Acceptability ●​ Durability ●​ Divisibility ●​ Portability ●​ Stability of Value ●​ Recognizability 6. Theories of Money ●​ Quantity Theory of Money: Value depends on supply relative to demand. ●​ Keynesian Theory: Money influences interest rates and investment. ●​ Modern Monetary Theory (MMT): Governments can issue currency to fund spending. 7. Role of Money in the Economy ●​ Facilitates trade and specialization. ●​ Influences inflation and deflation. ●​ Impacts monetary policy and interest rates. ●​ Shapes global financial systems. 8. Modern Trends in Money ●​ Digital Wallets: Apple Pay, Google Pay. ●​ Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC): State-backed digital money. ●​ Cryptocurrency & Blockchain: Decentralized finance (DeFi). ●​ Cashless Societies: Increasing reliance on electronic transactions. 9. Challenges and Future of Money ●​ Inflation and currency devaluation. ●​ Cybersecurity risks in digital money. ●​ Regulation of cryptocurrencies. ●​ Potential shift toward global digital currencies. 10. Conclusion Money has evolved from simple barter to complex digital systems. Its essence remains the same: a tool to facilitate exchange, measure value, and store wealth.
